name: Nymphaeaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project water lilies as rooted rhizomatous aquatics with long-petioled floating/emergent leaves and solitary many-parted flowers, then separate Nymphaea from Nuphar by leaf venation, flower presentation, petal visibility and stigmatic-disk architecture.

project_scope.selection_mode: Nymphaea odorata + source Nuphar lutea subsp. advena reconciled to Nuphar advena
project_scope.note: Both current species are accepted and native-range treatments include Texas. The source Nuphar infraspecific name is synonym provenance, not a separate current taxon.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the leaf attachment and the flower. Project Nymphaeaceae are rooted rhizomatous aquatics with long petioles, floating or emergent blades with a basal sinus, and solitary flowers with numerous stamens.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Perennial aquatic herbs rooted by rhizomes. Leaves arise on long petioles; blades are usually broad and floating or emergent, with the petiole attaching at the basal sinus rather than centrally peltate as in lotus.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers are solitary and many-parted, with numerous stamens and multiple petals or petaloid organs. Project genera differ strongly: Nymphaea has a spreading showy flower with numerous obvious petals grading toward stamens, while Nuphar has a more globose yellow flower dominated visually by sepals and tiny stamenlike petals.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Project fruits remain associated with the floral axis rather than forming lotus's enlarged showerhead receptacle; Nymphaea fruits mature on recurved/coiled peduncles, while Nuphar produces a leathery many-seeded fruit with a broad stigmatic disk.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Basal-sinus floating leaf + many-stamen water-lily flower = Nymphaeaceae. Then split Nymphaea versus Nuphar by flower shape and venation.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: leaf attachment → Nymphaea flower → Nuphar flower → venation split → stigmatic disk → fruit/peduncle → lotus comparison → taxonomy card
visual_lesson.intro: Water-lily and lotus can look similar from shore, but their leaf attachment and fruit architecture tell completely different evolutionary stories.

steps.title: 1 · Check where the petiole meets the blade
steps.look_for: The petiole reaches the blade at the basal notch/sinus rather than the center of the blade.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fastest whole-leaf split from peltate Nelumbo.

steps.title: 2 · Nymphaea door: spreading petal-rich flower
steps.look_for: Floating white flower with 4 green sepals and many conspicuous white petals grading inward toward numerous yellow stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: The obvious petal-to-stamen transition is the best visual Nymphaea cue.

steps.title: 3 · Nuphar door: sepals dominate
steps.look_for: Yellow globose/cup-shaped flower in which 5-9 thick sepals dominate the display; true petals are numerous but small and stamenlike.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents treating every yellow water-lily flower as a lotus or Nymphaea.

steps.title: 4 · Use venation as a genus check
steps.look_for: Nymphaea has strongly radiating/palmate primary veins; Nuphar has a more pinnate framework with several parallel basal veins along the midrib region.
steps.why_it_matters: Allows genus recognition even when flowers are absent.

steps.title: 5 · Find the stigmatic disk
steps.look_for: A broad disk at the center of the flower with radiating stigmatic lines/rays; Nuphar's disk is especially conspicuous atop the ovary.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes the central floral architecture understandable rather than treating it as an anonymous yellow disk.

steps.title: 6 · Follow Nymphaea below the surface after flowering
steps.look_for: Flower stalk curves or coils, drawing the developing fruit below the water.
steps.why_it_matters: A memorable reproductive sequence not shared with lotus.

steps.title: 7 · Water-lily vs lotus
steps.look_for: Nymphaeaceae petiole attaches at a basal sinus and flowers lack the lotus showerhead receptacle; Nelumbo leaves are centrally peltate and fruits sit in separate pits of an enlarged receptacle.
steps.why_it_matters: Corrects one of the most common aquatic-plant family confusions.

steps.title: 8 · Fix the spatterdock name
steps.look_for: Nuphar lutea subsp. advena → accepted Nuphar advena.
steps.why_it_matters: Keeps the Hays source record connected to the current backbone without duplicate taxa.

comparisons.title: Nymphaeaceae vs Nelumbonaceae
comparisons.rule: Water-lilies have leaves attached at the basal sinus and many-parted flowers without a showerhead fruiting receptacle. Lotus has centrally peltate leaves and separate carpels embedded in a broad flat-topped receptacle.

comparisons.title: Nymphaeaceae vs Ceratophyllaceae
comparisons.rule: Water-lilies are rooted rhizomatous plants with broad floating/emergent leaves and showy flowers. Ceratophyllum is rootless and fully submerged with whorled forked leaves and tiny perianthless flowers.

comparisons.title: Nymphaea vs Nuphar
comparisons.rule: Nymphaea = spreading flower with many obvious petals and radiating leaf venation. Nuphar = more globose yellow flower dominated by thick sepals, tiny petals, and more pinnate leaf venation.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use 'floating round leaf' alone. Lotus can also produce floating leaves, and Nuphar can produce emergent leaves. Petiole attachment, venation, and floral/fruit architecture are safer.

genera.fast_cue: basal-sinus leaf + spreading flower with many conspicuous petals grading into stamens
basal-sinus leaf + yellow globose flower dominated by thick sepals + broad stigmatic disk
